name: TimeBridge cross-contract signature-domain collision
summary: TimeToken.mint verified validator signatures over (sender, fromChainId, chainid, lockId, amount) without the contract address. The CGU bridge on BNB Chain signed the same message with the same validators, so the attacker replayed CGU unlock signatures on TimeToken to mint 519,000 unbacked TIME and sold it into the TIME/WBNB pair.
notes: The validator set and its size of two were final three days after deployment (2021) and the CGU bridge has existed since November 2021, so the deployment is the reset; the CGU bridge is the signature source, not a contract the anchor executed.

The minted TIME had no backing and its sale crashed the only pool, so loss is the attacker's realised proceeds (rule 15): the WBNB the TIME/WBNB pair paid out in the two sales (refs), not the ~$872K nominal mint value.
